newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina Electric nuke cuts power for repair.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina Electric nuke cuts power for repair.

text.p: South Carolina Electric and Gas Co's 960 megawatt Summer nuclear power plant has reduced electrical output for repairs, a company spokesman said Wednesday.
The Parr, S.C., unit was operating at near 40 percent of capacity as of early Wednesday, said spokesman Brian Duncan.
Power output was expected to be taken down to near 35 percent Wednesday while the company made repairs to a generator, the spokesman said.
"Barring any unforeseen events, we should start ramping up production tomorrow," Duncan said.
South Carolina, a unit of SCANA Corp, is the operator and has a two-thirds ownership in the Summer plant. The remaining one-third owning interest is held by Santee Cooper.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
